name: Curved Roller Conveyor

innerRadius.label: Inner radius (m)
innerRadius.desc: Radius of the INNER edge of the curve. The outer edge sits this plus the width away, so a tight inner radius on a wide bed makes a sharply banked turn that product can jam on.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Bed width, measured across the curve from the inner edge to the outer one.

frameHeight.label: Frame height (m)
frameHeight.desc: Depth of the side frame channel below the rollers. Set it to the Frame height of the conveyor this bed butts against so the two frames line up at the joint. The legs shorten or lengthen to meet the frame bottom; the deck height does not move.

sweepDeg.label: Sweep (°)
sweepDeg.desc: How far the curve turns. 90 degrees is the usual corner; 180 turns a lane back on itself. The snap ends move with this, so a neighbour re-snaps to the new tangent rather than needing to be dragged.

fpmUnits.label: PLC speed in FPM
fpmUnits.desc: The unit the PLC commands this conveyor in. On: feet per minute. Off: metres per second. The speed tag is a REAL either way, so switching changes what its value means and never how the program declares it. Set by the scene Units (Scene Properties), which switch every conveyor together, so the Inspector does not show it. A conveyor saved before this switch existed is in metres per second.

speedFpm.label: Speed
speedFpm.desc: Surface speed in feet per minute. Negative runs it backwards. A program can command this through the FPM speed tag below.

speed.label: Speed
speed.desc: Surface speed at the centreline of the curve; the outer edge moves faster, which carries a box round square. Negative reverses flow, the ONLY way to turn a curve around (spinning it would swap its inner and outer radius).

accelTime.label: Accel time
accelTime.desc: How long the drive takes to bring the conveyor from stopped up to its rated speed (the speed that reads 30, under Comms > Feedback), like the acceleration time set on a VFD. A smaller change takes proportionally less. 0 starts instantly.

decelTime.label: Decel time
decelTime.desc: How long the drive takes to bring the conveyor from rated speed down to a stop. Cargo keeps travelling while it does, so a box stopped at a photo-eye ends up past it. 0 stops instantly.

innerGuard.label: Inner guard
innerGuard.desc: Guard wall along the INNER edge of the curve. A real barrier, so turning it off lets cargo cut the corner and leave the bed.

outerGuard.label: Outer guard
outerGuard.desc: Guard wall along the OUTER edge, which is the one centrifugal drift pushes product against. A real barrier - turning it off is how you let product leave on the outside of a turn.

guardHoles.label: Guard holes [θ rad, y m, side ±1]
guardHoles.desc: Where sensor beams cross the side guards. Worked out by the host from the scene; not for editing.

standHeight.label: Stand height (m)
standHeight.desc: Height of the deck above whatever is beneath it, which sets the leg length. The host fills this in when you drop or snap the conveyor, so the legs reach the floor - or a platform crossing underneath - without you measuring. Pin it by hand when you want a deliberate height.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Connect this conveyor to a PLC program. Its tags appear once this is on.

speedTag.label: Speed tag (m/s)
speedTag.desc: The program commands surface speed here, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0 - so a half-wired conveyor sits still rather than running at its authored speed.

speedFpmTag.label: Speed tag (FPM)
speedFpmTag.desc: The program commands surface speed here in feet per minute, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Once BOUND this takes over even if no program writes it, so an unwritten tag holds the conveyor at 0.

runTag.label: Run tag (rollers run while true)
runTag.desc: Start/stop gate: false forces the speed to 0 whatever the setpoint says. Unlike the speed tag, this only takes effect once a program actually DRIVES it, so binding it alone will not stop the bed.

runningTag.label: Running tag (true while moving)
runningTag.desc: Feedback the conveyor publishes for the program to read: true whenever it is actually moving. This is the EFFECTIVE speed, gates included, so a run tag holding it at zero reads false here.

speedAt30.label: Speed that reads 30 (m/s)
speedAt30.desc: The surface speed this conveyor reaches when its drive turns at 30. It scales the velocity tag: running at exactly this speed reads 30.

speedAt30Fpm.label: Speed that reads 30 (FPM)
speedAt30Fpm.desc: The surface speed, in feet per minute, this conveyor reaches when its drive turns at 30. It scales the velocity tag: running at exactly this speed reads 30.

velocityTag.label: Velocity tag (30 at the speed above)
velocityTag.desc: Drive feedback the program reads: the effective speed as a share of the speed at 30 revolutions, times 30. Stopped reads 0, and a run tag holding the conveyor still counts as stopped.

inchesPerPulse.label: Travel per pulse (in)
inchesPerPulse.desc: How far the surface travels between pulses on the pulse tag. A pulse cannot be finer than one simulation step, so a fast conveyor at a fine pitch needs a higher project simHz.

pulseTag.label: Pulse tag (one per pitch)
pulseTag.desc: An encoder for the program to count: TRUE for one simulation step each time the surface has travelled the inches above, in either direction, and FALSE otherwise.

encoderTag.label: Encoder tag (travel, m)
encoderTag.desc: Odometer of surface travel in metres, integrated on sim time: it climbs while the conveyor runs forward and counts back while it reverses. Latch it when a photo-eye sees a box, then act once it has advanced a known distance - the standard way to track product without a sensor at every station.
